bg: zephaniah

Jehovah has concealed, or Jehovah of darkness. (1.) The son of Cushi, and great-grandson of Hezekiah, and the ninth in the order of the minor prophets. He prophesied in the days of Josiah, king of Judah (B.C. 641-610), and was contemporary with Jeremiah, with whom he had much in common.
Jerusalem

Jerusalem, if not actually in the centre of Palestine, was yet virtually so. "It was on the ridge, the broadest and most strongly-marked ridge of the backbone of the complicated hills which extend through the whole country from the plain of Esdraelon to the desert."
Hold
A fortress, the name given to David's lurking-places (1 Sam. 22:4, 5; 24:22).
Zephaniah
The ninth in order of the twelve minor prophets. His pedigree is traced to his fourth ancestor, Hezekiah, (Zephaniah 1:1) supposed to be the celebrated king of that name.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Threatenings against sinners (vv. 1–6); More threatenings (vv. 7–13); Distress from the approaching judgments (vv. 14–18). People named: Zephaniah, Gedaliah, Amariah, Josiah, Amon, Chemarims. Places: Judah, Jerusalem, Hold, Maktesh.
ch.mh: Ruin is coming, utter ruin; destruction from the Almighty.
q: Read verses 1–6 (Threatenings against sinners). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 7–13 (More threatenings), what do you learn about judgment?
Verse 18 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Ezekiel 7:19. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Zephaniah’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of family and generations in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Zephaniah?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us flee from the wrath to come, and choose the good part that shall never be taken from us; then we shall be prepared for every event; nothing shall separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
ch.a: Let the seriousness of God's judgment move you to examine your ways and to pray for others.

bg: zephaniah

Jehovah has concealed, or Jehovah of darkness. (1.) The son of Cushi, and great-grandson of Hezekiah, and the ninth in the order of the minor prophets. He prophesied in the days of Josiah, king of Judah (B.C. 641-610), and was contemporary with Jeremiah, with whom he had much in common.
Ashkelon
Askelon=Ascalon, was one of the five cities of the Philistines (Josh. 13:3; 1 Sam. 6:17). It stood on the shore of the Mediterranean, 12 miles north of Gaza.
Gaza

Called also Azzah, which is its Hebrew name (Deut. 2:23; 1 Kings 4:24; Jer. 25:20), strong, a city on the Mediterranean shore, remarkable for its early importance as the chief centre of a great commercial traffic with Egypt. It is one of the oldest cities of the world (Gen. 10:19; Josh. 15:47).
Ekron

Firm-rooted, the most northerly of the five towns belonging to the lords of the Philistines, about 11 miles north of Gath. It was assigned to Judah (Josh. 13:3), and afterwards to Dan (19:43), but came again into the full possession of the Philistines (1 Sam. 5:10).
ch.s: This chapter covers: An exhortation to repentance (vv. 1–3); Judgments upon other nations (vv. 4–15). People named: Moab, Ammon, Ashdod, Assyria. Places: Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, Canaan, Philistines.
ch.mh: The prophet calls to national repentance, as the only way to prevent national ruin.
q: Read verses 1–3 (An exhortation to repentance). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 4–15 (Judgments upon other nations), what do you learn about judgment?
Verse 3 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Amos 5:14–15. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Moab’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of worship and praise in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Zephaniah?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us improve our advantages, and expect the performance of every promise, praying that our Father's name may be hallowed every where, over all the earth.
ch.a: Let the seriousness of God's judgment move you to examine your ways and to pray for others.

bg: zephaniah

Jehovah has concealed, or Jehovah of darkness. (1.) The son of Cushi, and great-grandson of Hezekiah, and the ninth in the order of the minor prophets. He prophesied in the days of Josiah, king of Judah (B.C. 641-610), and was contemporary with Jeremiah, with whom he had much in common.
Jerusalem

Jerusalem, if not actually in the centre of Palestine, was yet virtually so. "It was on the ridge, the broadest and most strongly-marked ridge of the backbone of the complicated hills which extend through the whole country from the plain of Esdraelon to the desert."
Ethiopia

Country of burnt faces; the Greek word by which the Hebrew Cush is rendered (Gen. 2:13; 2 Kings 19:9; Esther 1:1; Job 28:19; Ps. 68:31; 87:4), a country which lay to the south of Egypt, beginning at Syene on the First Cataract (Ezek. 29:10; 30:6), and extending to beyond the confluence of the White and Blue Nile. It corresponds generally with what is now known as the Soudan (i.e., the land of the blacks).
ch.s: This chapter covers: Further reproofs for sin (vv. 1–7); Encouragement to look for mercy (vv. 8–13); Promises of future favour and prosperity (vv. 14–20). People named: Ethiopia. Places: Zion, Jerusalem.
ch.mh: The holy God hates sin most in those nearest to him.
q: Read verses 1–7 (Further reproofs for sin). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 8–13 (Encouragement to look for mercy), what do you learn about worship and praise?
Verse 19 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Isaiah 49:25–26. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Ethiopia’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of sin and repentance in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Zephaniah?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Write down three things this chapter shows about God and thank Him for each.
